generator.params.note: Wikipedia, Date palm (read 2026-10-14): up to 30 m, single or in a clump of stems from one root system; leaves 4 to 6 m long (frond_length 4.8), spined on the petiole, pinnate with about 150 leaflets (38 pieces of rachis, about 76 a side), the leaflets 30 cm long and 2 cm wide (leaflet_length 0.07 of the frond, cards of aspect 0.07); a crown 6 to 10 m across. Set by eye from general knowledge of the species: a rough trunk clothed in old leaf bases, stiff grey-green fronds whose leaflets stand in a V and 15 degrees above and below it, the oldest hanging 20 degrees lower over their life, and offshoots at the base. Not fitted to measurements. A frond rises from the spear to its spreading angle over half a year (open_years 0.5): at 1.2 years the crown's newest eighteen fronds stood near upright, a shaving brush, where photographs show one or two spears above a spreading crown.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of the species: about 10 m at 30 years and 20 m at 60. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: glaucous grey-green fronds, brown leaf bases. Shades as linear light (2026-10-16): fronds a glaucous grey-green [0.13, 0.18, 0.15], boots and dead fronds mid brown, the trunk a brown-grey, the petiole and rachis a glaucous yellowish grey-green with the leaflets (leaf_axis), not the palm family's lime; at [0.33, 0.42, 0.36] the fronds drew near white.
